correctness.rationale: An acyclic orientation has maximum directed reachability at most 4 when a matching edge occurs and n>=3, at most 3 for m=0 or n=2, at most 2 for n=1. Koana--Oh--Yoneda Theorem 3.1 makes these stable upper bounds. An explicit fixed ranking of the 5-vertex induced obstruction makes all 12 proper 3-colour assignments carry a mutual-envy pair. With Koana--Oh--Yoneda subgraph monotonicity and elementary triangle/K2 and K2,n lower bounds this proves every case. A separate Grundy proof uses at most two neighbour colours in the matching-plus-isolates part. A deterministic exhaustive enumeration over precisely 7776 preference profiles and 12 proper assignments per profile, tested by DFS and transitive closure, gives 624 (576 unavoidable mutual, 48 longer cycles essential). Both direct tests and analytic proof have been reconstructed and replayed.

value.rationale: The exact sharp four-colour threshold after a single within-part matching edge identifies a structural discontinuity in a new preference-aware graph invariant. Its witness is fixed, independent of graph order, despite the ordinary Grundy lower bound staying at three. On the minimal obstruction the 624/576/48 exact breakdown detects a substantial distinction between mutual envy and blocking cycles of length at least three, relevant to proposed stability tests.
